## What to build

Find out why Redline changes or deletes sentences that carry a deliberate epistemic limit, and why it makes unreported changes of taste to a clean text, and correct it without giving Redline the source.

In the Claude-family evaluation for #362, four drafts that Write had delivered were given to a source-blind `/redline --output=response input.md`. Redline loads nothing #362 changed. Judged against R1 of `docs/evaluation/corpus/editorial-quality/README.md`:

- `column-sv-r2`, R1 fail: two whole sentences deleted from a clean text, "Det här är en iakttagelse av ett dokument, inte en scen från ett visst möte." and "Det är min reflektion, inte något jag har mätt hos andra." Both deletions were reported accurately. Neither repaired a visible defect; each removed a hedge and so changed a claim's scope and strength. Both are the source's own caveats, near verbatim.
- `opinion-en_GB-r1`, R1 fail: ten differences from the input, one the repair of a visible defect and nine of taste (re-paragraphing, "channel" to "route", a recast closing line, "We" to "Öppna beslut", "the administration" to "the officers"). None was reported; the account says the re-review found nothing and no claim was removed.
- `opinion-en_GB-r2`, R1 pass, with a misdescription: "We make no claim to have funded or costed that trial" became "We have not costed that trial", and the account calls the qualification "preserved in full". That turns a withheld claim into a denial, the boundary #349 established.
- `column-sv-r1`, R1 pass: one tautological restatement removed and reported; the caveat itself kept.

Redline cannot know what a source required, and must not be given the source. But a sentence that limits what is claimed ("not measured", "makes no claim to", "an observation of the document, not a scene") is visible as such in the text alone, and removing or hardening it changes what the text asserts, which R1 already forbids outside a finding. The account must also report every change it made to what a claim says.

Evidence: `docs/evaluation/editorial-362/runs/*/redline/` (`work/input.md`, `response.md`, `judgement.md`) and `docs/evaluation/records/redline-claude-2026-09-20-362.md`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The cause is diagnosed from Redline's loaded resources and a neutral replay of the four inputs above, before any instruction changes.
- [ ] In a frozen provider-native evaluation, the four inputs above are each reviewed at least twice; no run deletes or hardens a sentence that limits what the text claims unless a reported finding names a visible defect in it, and every change to what a claim says appears in the account.
- [ ] Established Redline controls that require a real removal or a real repair still pass; clean texts are returned unchanged or with mechanical corrections only.
- [ ] No source material is supplied to Redline in any run.
- [ ] The four checks in `CONTRIBUTING.md` pass and the catalog is regenerated.

## Readiness addendum, 2026-09-20

This comment is the requirement wherever it touches the body. Where it contradicts the body, the addendum stands; where it is silent, the body stands. The readiness check found two stops in the third acceptance criterion and a number of costs, and each is settled below. Nothing here is a question for the builder.

### Two corrections to the body

The body says of `opinion-en_GB-r1`: "ten differences from the input, one the repair of a visible defect and nine of taste (re-paragraphing, "channel" to "route", a recast closing line, "We" to "Öppna beslut", "the administration" to "the officers")". That is not how the run's own judgement classes them. `docs/evaluation/editorial-362/runs/opinion-en_GB-r1/redline/judgement.md` classes four of the ten as *a change to what the claim says* — `#2` and `#7`, the administration becoming the officers, and `#4` and `#10`, channel becoming route — one as house-style mechanics (`#6`, a dropped serial comma), and one as consequent on another change (`#7`'s verb agreement), leaving six of taste. Use the judgement's classification, not the body's count: the second half of the criterion below turns on what a change to a claim is, and four of these are that rather than taste.

The body was written against `89f83bdc`. Since then the record it cites has had its `defects filed` fields changed to name this issue, and `docs/evaluation/editorial-362/README.md` has gained the paragraph naming #376, #377 and #378 as filed. Nothing else the body relies on moved: the four inputs, the four judgements, R1 and Redline's loaded resources are as the body describes them. The builder works against `main` as it stands when it starts and re-reads each surface named below before editing it.

### Where the change goes

The diagnostic rule — that a sentence limiting what the text claims is not removed or weakened to taste — goes in `skills/kntnt/library/references/editorial/base.review.md`. Only Redline loads that file: its `SKILL.md` step 5 and its `references/correction.md` name it, Write's `SKILL.md` step 5 loads no review half, and Unslop loads `anti-slop.md` and a language scope only. It is written as a diagnostic of requirements `base.md` already states — "Preserve the state of knowledge: what is unknown or unclaimed is not thereby known not to have happened", "Keep uncertainty where it exists and certainty where it is warranted", and "Preserve chronology, scope and qualifications wherever a claim appears" — so it introduces no independent target, which `skills/kntnt/library/references/editorial/README.md` forbids a review half from doing. The builder chooses its wording and says in the commit why the rule sits there rather than in the base half.

Nothing goes in `base.md`. A rule that must also reach Write is a separate ticket, filed `needs-triage` and naming this one; it is not built here, and no Write run is owed by this ticket.

The account duty, and the permission it currently rests on, are Redline's own procedure and live in Redline's shipped files, as `docs/rules/docs.md` requires of a rule governing one Skill's behaviour. The sentence to narrow is in `skills/editorial/redline/SKILL.md` step 7: "Where the finding named the whole claim as the defect, its removal may stand, but the delivery still names the claim that went." That is the permission the failing run invoked, in as many words — `docs/evaluation/editorial-362/runs/column-sv-r2/redline/response.md` reads "I båda fallen pekade fyndet ut hela meningen som defekten, och borttagningen fick därför stå". A criterion that left that sentence standing would be met by a run reproducing the defect exactly.

### The sweep

These surfaces assert the account duty as removals-only, or the whole-passage permission, and are swept in the same change, as `docs/rules/docs.md` requires. The list is exhaustive as of the commit named at the foot of this comment:

- `skills/editorial/redline/SKILL.md`, steps 7 and 11.
- `skills/editorial/redline/help.md`: "A claim-losing correction is rejected and restored, and every removed claim is reported", and "every removed claim remains visible".
- `skills/editorial/redline/references/correction.md`: the paragraphs headed **What a repair may take with it, and what it may not** and **What you return**, and the paragraph opening "Before you return the text, compare it before and after, claim by claim."
- `skills/kntnt/library/references/editorial/base.review.md`: "A claim removed because the finding named that claim itself remains part of the removal account."

No test pins that prose, so the suite will not flag a surface left behind; the catalog digests do change, so it is regenerated. No decision record is owed: reversible prose inside one Skill's contract fails all three of the criteria `docs/rules/docs.md` sets for a record. If the builder judges otherwise, the record takes the next free number at the time of writing and the commit says which number it took.

### What the terms mean

A **limiting sentence** is a sentence or clause whose work in the text is to bound what the text asserts: that something is not measured, not claimed, not witnessed or not general, or that the text is an observation of a document rather than a scene from an occasion.

A **change to what a claim says** is a difference that alters a claim's strength, subject, scope, modality, attribution or chronology. The first four are already the frozen vocabulary of `docs/evaluation/editorial-362/runs/redline-judge-brief.md`; attribution and chronology are added because two of `opinion-en_GB-r1`'s changes moved a claim's actor and no judge was asked to call that a claim change.

**Hardening** is any change that raises what the text asserts. The judge must test for these four forms, and records and names any fifth it finds:

1. A refusal to assert becomes an assertion — "We make no claim to have costed that trial" to "We have not costed that trial".
2. A disclaimer covering two things comes back covering one — the dropped "funded or" in the same sentence.
3. A sentence whose only work is to limit is deleted outright.
4. A claim's subject or attribution moves to a different actor — "the administration" to "the officers".

### The escape clause

A deletion or weakening of a limiting sentence is permitted only where the account reports a finding naming a defect in that sentence which a judge can verify from the input text alone, independently of the account's assertion, and only in these two classes:

- **(a)** the sentence states a limit another retained sentence already states in full — the `column-sv-r1` case, where "Jag har inte mätt det här hos andra, och jag påstår inget om möten i allmänhet." remained; or
- **(b)** the sentence contradicts another passage of the same text.

A finding that names the whole sentence as the defect without naming a defect inside it is not one of these and licenses nothing. This is the same narrowing the `SKILL.md` sentence above receives, so the shipped contract and the criterion say one thing.

### How the evaluation is run

Family: Claude. `docs/evaluation/protocol.md` forbids a Claude session from driving a Codex Harness, so no GPT harness or GPT model is started here; a GPT-family retest is Thomas's own step, ordered separately on #362.

Staging is the method frozen in `docs/evaluation/editorial-362/runs/plan.md`, with `docs/evaluation/editorial-362/runs/redline-turn.md` as the turn and `docs/evaluation/editorial-362/runs/redline-judge-brief.md` as the judge brief: a byte copy of the Skills the run needs beside `skills/kntnt` in the session scratchpad, one fresh subagent per invocation, the Formal Invocation carried verbatim, and a `sha256` inventory before and after. The inventory covers every writable location staged for the run, including the whole working copy and any separate Harness scratch area, as `docs/evaluation/protocol.md` requires — not the run directory and staged install alone.

Every run, every correction agent it starts and every judge is a fresh `claude-opus-5` subagent at high deliberation, as `docs/evaluation/editorial-362/README.md` records for the runs this ticket is filed from. A builder on a weaker seat measures its own seat instead of the product.

Two independent judges per artefact wherever a criterion turns on a judgement, each blind to the expected answer; where they split, both classes are recorded and neither judge is an oracle. One judge suffices for a mechanical check — a diff, a count, the presence of a report.

The corpus matrix's `T1` and `R2` are answerable only from a Harness trace, and a session cannot read the transcript of a subagent it started. Both are recorded `skipped` with that reason. Nothing here claims either passed and nothing fails for lacking them.

The evaluation lives at `docs/evaluation/editorial-377/`: a plan, a results file and a run tree, frozen before the first run and not edited afterwards. The record goes under `docs/evaluation/records/` in the protocol's format, named as `docs/evaluation/protocol.md` says — the date form, taking this issue after the date, because a `redline`/`claude` record already exists for 2026-09-20 — and is listed in `docs/evaluation/records/README.md`.

### The controls

Ten artefacts under `docs/evaluation/corpus/editorial-quality/controls/`, exhaustive for this ticket. Those that require a real removal or a real repair: `article-flawed`, `case-study-flawed`, `column-flawed`, `opinion-flawed`, `web-copy-flawed`. The clean ones: `article-clean`, `case-study-clean`, `column-clean`, `opinion-clean`, `web-copy-clean`. `report-pac` and the metadata and precedence controls are not this ticket's.

Each is run once, staged and invoked as the corpus's *Redline controls* section says — only the linked artifact copied to `input.md`, then `/redline --genre=<genre> --language=<locale> --output=response input.md` with that row's genre and locale, `sv` throughout except `web-copy-flawed`, which is `en_US`. Each is judged on `R1` alone, beside the protocol's side-effect check read from the inventory; every other criterion the corpus applies to a control run is recorded `skipped`, naming `R1` as this ticket's criterion, with `T1` and `R2` skipped for the trace reason above.

"Still pass" is not a comparison, because there is nothing in this family to compare with: the only records covering these controls are `redline-gpt-2026-09-19-338-controls-genres.md` and `redline-gpt-2026-09-19-346-controls-genres.md`, both GPT-family, and the protocol forbids re-running them here. The standard is each control's own frozen expectation in the corpus table. Where a control misses it, the builder re-runs that one control once against the pre-change wording: a miss present in both arms is a pre-existing failure, recorded as measured and filed `needs-triage` naming this ticket, and it does not block this one.

The body's "clean texts are returned unchanged or with mechanical corrections only" is scoped to exactly the five `*-clean` artefacts named above. It does not reach the four evaluation inputs, which the criterion above it governs alone. That is what stops it contradicting them: the body itself records `column-sv-r1` as a pass for deleting a whole sentence from a text it calls clean, and that run remains the behaviour this ticket wants.

### The frontmatter damage is not this ticket's

The body says of `column-sv-r2`: "two whole sentences deleted from a clean text". A fourth difference exists that the body does not mention. The returned artifact in `docs/evaluation/editorial-362/runs/column-sv-r2/redline/response.md` opens its frontmatter with `---` followed by a blank line, where that run's `redline/work/input.md` has `---` and then `kntnt:` immediately; the blank line breaks the block. That run's `redline/judgement.md` records it as "Formatting damage" and "Not mentioned in the account". The builder files it as its own `needs-triage` issue naming this ticket, neither fixes it nor counts it here, and a new run that repeats it fails no criterion of this ticket.

### Scale, and the exit when a measurement is unfavourable

Twenty-two Redline invocations: four pre-change replays, eight post-change runs, ten controls. Each starts its own correction agent and one nested Proofread. About thirty-six judge subagents, two per artefact where a criterion turns on a judgement. A builder planning materially more than that has widened the ticket.

For each criterion that measures a model rather than a file, the builder gets one revise-and-remeasure round, which adds at most eight runs and sixteen judges. If the criterion is still unmet, the measured result is recorded as measured, the shipped wording is left as the better of the two arms, the remaining miss is filed as its own `needs-triage` issue naming this ticket, and this ticket is done. Unbounded iteration is not the work. No criterion is softened and no frozen matrix, plan or fixture is edited to fit a result.

### Acceptance criteria

These replace the body's first three criteria. The body's fourth — no source material supplied to Redline in any run — and its fifth — the four checks in `CONTRIBUTING.md` pass and the catalog is regenerated — stay in force exactly as filed.

Replacing the first:

- [ ] `docs/evaluation/editorial-377/diagnosis.md` is committed in its own commit, before any commit that changes a shipped file, and carries: one neutral replay of each of the four named inputs, with no hint of the defect in the turn; every difference between each `work/input.md` and its returned text, classed in the vocabulary above; and, for every difference that deletes or weakens a limiting sentence or that the account does not report, the quoted sentence of a loaded resource that authorised it.

Replacing the second:

- [ ] The plan and criteria for the evaluation are committed under `docs/evaluation/editorial-377/` before its first run, and nothing frozen there is edited afterwards.
- [ ] Each of the four named inputs is reviewed twice after the change. In no run is a limiting sentence deleted or hardened unless the account reports a finding of class (a) or (b), verified by a judge from the input alone; and in every run the account names every change to what a claim says.
- [ ] `skills/editorial/redline/SKILL.md` no longer permits a removal on the ground that the finding named the whole claim as the defect, and its delivery duty covers changed claims rather than removals alone.
- [ ] The record is under `docs/evaluation/records/`, named as `docs/evaluation/protocol.md` says, and listed in `docs/evaluation/records/README.md`.

Replacing the third:

- [ ] `article-flawed`, `case-study-flawed`, `column-flawed`, `opinion-flawed` and `web-copy-flawed` are each run once and each meets its frozen expectation in the corpus table on `R1`.
- [ ] `article-clean`, `case-study-clean`, `column-clean`, `opinion-clean` and `web-copy-clean` are each run once and each comes back unchanged or with mechanical corrections only.

Added:

- [ ] Every surface named under *The sweep* states the account duty as it now stands.
- [ ] The `column-sv-r2` frontmatter damage is filed as a `needs-triage` issue naming this ticket. Where the work finds a rule that must also reach `base.md`, and so Write, that rule is filed the same way; where it finds none, the commit says so.

## Second readiness addendum, 2026-09-20

This comment is the requirement wherever it touches the body or the readiness addendum above it. Where it contradicts either, this comment stands; where it is silent, they stand in the order they were written. A second readiness check returned **No** on the addendum's third criterion and on the sweep. All three stops are one failure repeated: a sentence that corrected the body's facts and then asserted its own, without being checked against the tree. Each is settled below, with the sentence it voids named. Nothing here is a question for the builder.

Everything asserted below was checked against `68f2b6e2`, a clean working tree.

---

### 1. The sweep list was not exhaustive. Unslop is in it, for one of the two rules

**Voided:** "The list is exhaustive as of the commit named at the foot of this comment." **Voided:** "The account duty, and the permission it currently rests on, are Redline's own procedure and live in Redline's shipped files, as `docs/rules/docs.md` requires of a rule governing one Skill's behaviour."

Both rules the ticket changes exist a second time under `skills/editorial/unslop/`, in the same words with *pattern* for *defect*. As of `68f2b6e2`:

- `skills/editorial/unslop/SKILL.md` step 7 ends "Where the finding named the whole claim as the pattern, its removal may stand, but the delivery still names the claim that went." — Redline's step 7 sentence with one word changed.
- `skills/editorial/unslop/SKILL.md` step 9 carries the removals-only delivery duty, as Redline's step 11 does.
- `skills/editorial/unslop/help.md` carries two sentences the sweep listed under Redline's `help.md`. "A claim-losing correction is rejected and restored, and every removed claim is reported." is the identical string in both files; "The Skill reports the findings separately, in the text's own language, and every removed claim remains visible." is the identical string in both files.
- `skills/editorial/unslop/references/correction.md` line 31 is **byte-identical** to `skills/editorial/redline/references/correction.md` line 31 — the paragraph opening "Before you return the text, compare it before and after, claim by claim.", which the sweep named. Its **What you return** paragraph carries the removals-only duty in the same words.

`docs/rules/docs.md` says to enumerate by what a surface asserts rather than by how it words it. Two files asserting one rule in identical bytes are one contract's surfaces whatever directory they sit in, and the two Skills share that prose because they share a dispatch: ADR-0178 records it at the line beginning "It is stated once, in the brief itself" — "The rule belongs to the Collection rather than to the Skill it was observed in, because both Skills that spend a Correction Budget dispatch from a brief carrying the user's text under the same words."

**The decision is per rule, because the ticket changes two things and only one of them has an Unslop analogue.**

**The account duty is swept into Unslop in the same change.** Widening "every removed claim" to cover every change to what a claim says costs Unslop nothing it does not already owe — its correction agent can substitute a word and move a claim's scope while removing a pattern exactly as Redline's can — and it keeps the byte-identical strings byte-identical. Unslop's `SKILL.md` steps 7 and 9, its `help.md` and its `references/correction.md` are swept in Unslop's own *pattern* vocabulary.

**The limiting-sentence narrowing is Redline's alone, and that is a scope decision rather than an omission.** Unslop loads `anti-slop.md` and a language scope and nothing else — verified: `base.review.md` is named only by `skills/editorial/redline/SKILL.md` step 5, by `skills/editorial/redline/references/correction.md`, and by `skills/kntnt/library/references/editorial/README.md`, nowhere else under `skills/`. `anti-slop.md` already excludes the case this ticket is about: "where a phrase is doing real work — a hedge that marks genuine doubt, a repetition that lands — the pattern is not present and nothing is changed." Unslop therefore never reaches a limiting sentence as a finding, and narrowing its permission would change what it does to an unattributable claim, which is the behaviour ADR-0120 settled and which nothing in this ticket re-measures.

That leaves one deliberate divergence, in a sentence that is byte-identical today: after the change Redline's step 7 permission is narrower than Unslop's. The commit says which Unslop sentence keeps the old wording and why, and a `needs-triage` issue naming this ticket asks whether Unslop's whole-passage permission needs the same narrowing, so the divergence is on the tracker rather than only in a commit message. That issue is filed, not built here.

---

### 2. Three tests pin that prose, and they pass today

**Voided:** "No test pins that prose, so the suite will not flag a surface left behind." That is false, and the suite is the body's fifth criterion, so a builder acting on it would have broken the build it is held to.

Three tests in `tests/test_kntnt.py`, at roughly lines 8405, 8428 and 8453 as of `68f2b6e2`, pin exactly the prose the sweep names, across both Skills, and all three pass on that commit:

- `test_re_review_rejects_and_reports_a_correction_that_loses_a_claim` loops over `(REDLINE, REDLINE_CORRECTION, REDLINE_HELP)` and `(UNSLOP, UNSLOP_CORRECTION, UNSLOP_HELP)` and asserts `"every removed claim"` in all six files, plus `"pre-round text artifact"` and `"reject the returned correction"` in both `SKILL.md` bodies.
- `test_a_correction_of_concentrated_patterns_preserves_each_claim` asserts `"before and after"` and `"every claim"` against both `references/correction.md` files — the paragraph the sweep names.
- `test_a_punctuation_repair_removes_the_defect_and_keeps_its_fact` pins the worked punctuation-joint case in both briefs.

**The decision:** the phrase `every removed claim` is preserved verbatim in all six files and **added to**, rather than replaced. The account duty becomes the removed claims *and* every change to what a claim says, in one sentence per surface, with the existing clause left standing.

`tests/test_kntnt.py` is a sweep surface and is named as one. `docs/rules/docs.md` counts a test's own name among a contract's surfaces, and the docstring of `test_re_review_rejects_and_reports_a_correction_that_loses_a_claim` states the duty as removals-only — "every removal remains visible in both the correction account and the run's delivery". Two changes there, and no others:

- The six-file loop gains an assertion that each of the six surfaces requires the changed-claim half of the duty, so the suite flags a surface left behind for the new half as it already does for the old one.
- That docstring gains the changed-claim half. The test's name is left exactly as it is: it still describes what the test checks.

No test is rewritten and no assertion is removed. A builder who finds that it cannot add the new duty without deleting `every removed claim` from a surface has widened the rule beyond what this ticket asks for.

---

### 3. One rule for what a change to a claim is, and it is the one the tree already ships

**Voided:** "A **change to what a claim says** is a difference that alters a claim's strength, subject, scope, modality, attribution or chronology." **Voided:** "Use the judgement's classification, not the body's count." **Voided:** "The first four are already the frozen vocabulary of `docs/evaluation/editorial-362/runs/redline-judge-brief.md`; attribution and chronology are added because two of `opinion-en_GB-r1`'s changes moved a claim's actor and no judge was asked to call that a claim change."

Those two instructions are not the same rule and they disagree on the run the criterion is measured against. The last of them is also wrong about the data: `docs/evaluation/editorial-362/runs/opinion-en_GB-r1/redline/judgement.md` classes `#2` and `#7` as "Change to what the claim says (subject)". The judge *was* asked, and did call it a claim change. The item it called taste is `#8`, and that is one, not two.

**The rule is the list the tree already ships**, at `skills/editorial/redline/references/correction.md` line 31 and `skills/editorial/unslop/references/correction.md` line 31, byte-identical as of `68f2b6e2`:

> Every claim you received must still appear with its **scope, certainty, attribution, chronology, causality and meaning** intact unless the finding named the whole claim as the defect.

That list, those six words, is the definition for this ticket — for the diagnosis, for `editorial-377`'s judge brief, and for the shipped account duty. The addendum's list was a seventh statement of a contract that already has one, in different words, and `docs/rules/docs.md` is against exactly that. The `redline-judge-brief.md` under `editorial-362` keeps its four-word vocabulary because it is frozen evidence of a finished run; `editorial-377` writes its own brief and uses the six.

**Applied item by item to the ten rows of `opinion-en_GB-r1`'s judgement table**, which is what the criterion turns on:

| # | Class under the one rule | Which element |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Taste | re-paragraphing, no wording touched |
| 2 | Change to what the claim says | attribution — the objection moves from the administration to the officers |
| 3 | Taste | "double administration" to "the duplicated work"; same motive, meaning intact |
| 4 | Change to what the claim says | scope — "channel" to "route" collapses the text's own distinction |
| 5 | **Change to what the claim says** | scope — "permanent" drops out, leaving "that decision" to carry it |
| 6 | Mechanical | dropped serial comma, optional in en_GB |
| 7 | Change to what the claim says | attribution, as `#2`; its "asks" to "ask" is consequent mechanics |
| 8 | **Change to what the claim says** | attribution — the disclaimer's utterer moves from the text's own voice to a named third party |
| 9 | Repair of a visible defect | the one change that would have earned a finding |
| 10 | Change to what the claim says | scope, as `#4` |

`#5` and `#8` are the two the judgement called taste and the one rule calls claim changes, and they are why the one rule is adopted rather than the judgement's classification. The judgement's own words support both: it writes "with a small scope loss" beside `#5`, and it lists `#8` under R1's per-item reporting as an unreported difference.

**The corrected rationale sentence**, replacing the voided one: the six-element list is adopted because it is the list the correction agent is already handed, and because it catches `#5` and `#8`, which the `editorial-362` judgement classed as taste under a four-word vocabulary that has no place for either.

**Hardening.** Forms 1, 2 and 3 stand exactly as written. Form 4 — "A claim's subject or attribution moves to a different actor" — is **voided from the hardening list**. Hardening is defined in the same comment as "any change that raises what the text asserts", and moving a claim's actor does not raise what is asserted. It is a change to what a claim says, the criterion covers it there, and leaving it under hardening would make that definition false in its own paragraph. The judge still tests for these three forms, and records and names any fourth it finds.

---

### 4. The costs

**C1 — the arithmetic.** **Voided:** "leaving six of taste." Four claim changes, one mechanical, one consequent and six of taste is twelve of ten and omits `#9`. The count is the table in section 3: six changes to what a claim says (`#2`, `#4`, `#5`, `#7`, `#8`, `#10`), one repair of a visible defect (`#9`), one mechanical (`#6`) with `#7`'s verb agreement consequent on a claim change, and two of taste (`#1`, `#3`). The body's "nine of taste" is voided by the same count.

**C2 — the clean controls have one standard, not two.** **Voided:** "each comes back unchanged or with mechanical corrections only," and the body's "clean texts are returned unchanged or with mechanical corrections only." The standard for a clean control is the same as for a flawed one: its own frozen expectation in the corpus's *Redline controls* table, judged on `R1`. Nothing in the corpus defines a mechanical correction for Redline, and Redline ends every run with a nested Proofread pass it does not control — `SKILL.md` step 5 forbids the review itself from loading mechanics guidance, and step 9 hands the whole mechanical pass to Proofread. `column-sv-r1` is the worked case: its em-dash to en-dash normalisation is a locale-mechanical correction, unreported, and the judgement is explicit that this is correct and does not bear on the verdict. A clean control that comes back with such corrections and meets its corpus row passes.

### The escape clause, as it now reads

This replaces the addendum's *The escape clause* section entire.

A deletion or weakening of a limiting sentence is permitted only where the account reports a finding naming a defect in that sentence which a judge can verify from the input text alone, independently of the account's assertion, and only in these two classes:

- **(a)** the limit that sentence states is still stated by a sentence the text retains, so that after the deletion the text bounds what it claims exactly as far as it did before. Which words carry the limit afterwards does not matter; what matters is that no surviving claim gains scope, certainty, attribution, chronology, causality or meaning. `column-sv-r1` is the case: the removed sentence's self-description went, and "Jag har inte mätt det här hos andra, och jag påstår inget om möten i allmänhet." carries the whole of its limiting work.
- **(b)** the sentence contradicts another passage of the same text.

A finding that names the whole sentence as the defect without naming a defect inside it is not one of these and licenses nothing.

### What the narrowing in `SKILL.md` step 7 is, and what it is not

The narrowing is **scoped to limiting sentences** and to nothing else. The whole-passage permission stands for every other claim, because the corpus requires it: `opinion-flawed`'s frozen expectation is that Redline detects and removes unsupported motives and a population inference, and `column-flawed`'s is that it removes sweeping and generic claims — each with a removal account. A blanket removal of that permission would fail two of the five flawed controls this ticket runs, in the same change that runs them. The shipped sentence and the escape clause above say one thing, and both say it about limiting sentences.
